To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated the functionality of the UV discharge and charging system, that we can measure the rate of charging of isolated test masses, that we can maintain the charge on isolated test masses near zero, and that we can measure charge on the test masses with a precision of about 0.01 electrons.
the UV discharge system is functional, that the UV discharge rate is proportional to the power, and that the test‐mass can be held at near zero charge without introducing excess force.

(1) we demonstrated that the test‐mass can be charged positively and negatively with the UV system, (2) the charging rates can be measured and are proportional to the UV light power, and (3) we demonstrated that a combination of light illumination of the test‐mas and the surrounding sensor can hold the test‐mass near zero charge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics and control of the test masses of the LISA mission.
the design and implementation of a system for charging and discharging of LISA Pathfinder test masses.
the development of a system to discharge charged test masses in LISA Pathfinder, which will allow for the first time to measure the force of the gravitational radiation from the test masses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UV discharge system has been demonstrated as a viable method to control charge on the LISA Pathfinder test masses.
the test‐masses are successfully charged and dischargeable using UV light, and this system can be used to maintain the test‐mass at a desired charge level.

the UV discharge system is functional and can be used to discharge the LISA and/or LISA Pathfinder test masses.
Testing the UV discharge system of LISA Pathfinder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the UV discharge system is functional and has the potential to discharge the test masses in the presence of a high background charge environment; it has been demonstrated that the test‐masses are charged and discharged in a manner consistent with the photoelectric effect; the test mass charge is held near zero by the combination of UV light illuminating the mass and the surrounding housing; the UV discharge system has no significant effect on the noise floor of the pendulum detection system.
the UV discharge system is a viable technique to maintain a constant test‐mass charge in space.
the UV discharge system is a robust, reliable, and effective means of discharging test masses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the UV discharge system is functional and that the UV discharge rate is proportional to UV power.
the test mass can be charged to a desired value and discharged at will using UV illumination.

we can demonstrate the functionality of the UV discharge mechanism and show that it is compatible with the LISA and LPF test mass sensors, and that the discharge mechanism does not add excess noise to the system.
